"g": "C",
       "when": "NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III.",
       "pref": "NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III. The best-adjusted individual-patient analysis sits here too: in 357 resections at 12 institutions, with 81 propensity-matched pairs, adjuvant therapy showed no survival benefit overall (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.51–1.56, P=0.69) and none within any stage stratum, while stage drove both treatment and outcome — adjuvant use rose from 17.4% in stage I to 64.0% in stage II and 74.0% in stage III, and median survival fell from 137 to 57 to 45 months. Adding radiotherapy conferred nothing against surgery alone (hazard ratio 0.77, 0.41–1.44, P=0.41) or against chemotherapy alone (1.58, 0.69–2.60, P=0.28), and recurrence was predominantly distant (38 of 58, 65.5%) rather than locoregional (11 of 58, 19.0%). The registry weight points the other way: NCCN's discussion reports that in 4,190 National Cancer Database cases adjuvant chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 47.2 against 35.5 months (hazard ratio 0.82, P<0.01) and adjuvant chemoradiation 38.1 against 31.0 months (0.84, P=0.02), with higher T and N stages appearing to benefit most, and two large meta-analyses of 71 studies with 8,280 patients and of 10 studies with 3,361 report clinical benefit.",
       "avoid": "All of the supportive evidence is registry and retrospective, and the confounding runs one way: NCCN records that in the studies finding no effect, adjuvant therapy was more frequently used in patients with more advanced disease. That biases towards finding no benefit in unadjusted analyses and towards finding benefit once stage is adjusted — which is exactly the pattern the literature shows, including inside ESPAC-3 itself. The propensity-matched null is not a clean negative either: matching discarded 195 of 357 patients, the matched intervals do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction, half the screened population (369 of 756) was excluded for unknown subtype, matching omitted grade, lymphovascular invasion, margin, CA 19-9 and year of surgery despite grade, lymphovascular invasion and margin all differing between treated and untreated patients, median follow-up of 34 months is shorter than the 57-month median survival, and the 17-year accrual is dominated by gemcitabine monotherapy so it cannot speak to modern multiagent therapy. Black race appeared as one of the strongest predictors of both death (hazard ratio 3.93, 95% CI 1.95–7.93) and treatment omission (odds ratio 0.26, 0.09–0.76), which signals access and socioeconomic confounding that no propensity model built on tumour variables can absorb.",
       "refs": [
        "22782416",
        "31141112"

files.old: {"16111953":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors state only that the findings 'suggest' a protective effect and that future large-scale studies are required to confirm the benefit","They note there are no data on how long the duct should be stented"],"critique":["Nineteen patients and three events cannot establish an effect. The nominally significant p = 0.02 comes from a 3-versus-0 comparison, and the intention-to-treat analysis the authors themselves perform is frankly negative (p = 0.3) - a result that should have been the headline rather than a mid-paper aside","Stopping early at an interim look triggered by a high event rate in the control arm is the classic route to an overestimated treatment effect; no alpha adjustment is applied, and the trial has roughly a fifth of its planned sample","The three analyses presented (per protocol excluding the failed placement, as-treated, intention-to-treat) give p = 0.05, 0.02 and 0.3 from 19 patients; reporting the most favourable as the result is selective","Single endoscopist, single centre, single operator technique - specifically en bloc snare without a submucosal cushion so as to include the sphincteric musculature - which the authors argue reduces later cannulation-related pancreatitis. The result therefore cannot be separated from one operator's method, and no learning-curve or centre-effect data exist","Patients were blinded but outcome ascertainment depended on patients reporting pain and then having enzymes checked; the endoscopist was necessarily unblinded, and whether the 24-hour telephone assessor's blinding was maintained for the stented patients who returned for fluoroscopy and stent removal is doubtful","Allocation by card from a sealed envelope without blocking or stratification produced unequal arms (11 vs 8) and a 9-year age difference between groups in a 19-patient trial; concealment by opaque envelope is weaker than central randomisation","The outcome window was only 24 hours, so delayed pancreatitis, bleeding, perforation, papillary stenosis and recurrence - the complications that matter over the longer term - were not captured at all","Electrosurgical generator changed during the study (Meditron to ERBE) and all three pancreatitis cases occurred with the ERBE device; generator is therefore confounded with time and potentially with allocation, and is not adjusted for","Pancreatitis was defined as threefold enzyme elevation with pain but enzymes were measured only in symptomatic patients, so asymptomatic hyperamylasaemia and milder events were differentially unascertained","The companion randomised trial in this depot (Lee 2016) found 18% versus 13% pancreatitis with wire-guided versus conventional papillectomy despite 100% stent success in the wire-guided arm, and the later ESGE guideline rates prophylactic stenting as moderate-quality evidence drawing on larger series - so this trial's 0% stented pancreatitis rate is almost certainly an artefact of its size"],"n":"19 patients enrolled and randomised (11 assigned to stent, 8 to no stent); final stent placement achieved in 10, so analysis compared 10 stented with 9 unstented patients","bottom_line":"The first and still most-cited randomised trial of prophylactic pancreatic stenting after snare ampullectomy, reporting 33% versus 0% pancreatitis, but it enrolled only 19 patients, was stopped early at an interim look, and lost statistical significance on its own intention-to-treat analysis - it is a signal consistent with a protective effect rather than proof of one.","funding":"Not stated"},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The paper carries no limitations section; the authors note instead that the optimal duration of biliary drainage has never been established and that a shorter period may not allow recovery of metabolic abnormalities while a longer one risks stent occlusion and bile-duct inflammation","They point out that four of five earlier randomised trials used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage and included both proximal and distal obstruction, entities now considered different diseases needing different treatment","They concede that, given the poor results with plastic stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with metal stents"],"critique":["The composite primary outcome counts drainage complications and surgical complications in the same tally, so a trial of whether drainage makes surgery safer is decided mainly by whether drainage itself causes harm. On the question clinicians actually ask - does jaundice at operation increase surgical risk? - the trial is null (47% vs 37%, RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.57-1.11), and that is the result buried in the secondary analysis","Plastic stents only. A 26% cholangitis rate and 30% stent-exchange rate are features of 10 Fr plastic endoprostheses left for 4-6 weeks; the trial cannot be read as evidence against short-course drainage or against self-expanding metal stents, which the authors themselves recommend for the neoadjuvant setting","Early surgery required guaranteed theatre capacity within a week at 13 hospitals; 3 patients crossed over to drainage because surgery could not be arranged in time. Outside a trial that logistic constraint is the usual reason drainage happens, so the comparison tests an idealised pathway","Noninferiority was the prespecified frame with a 10 percentage-point margin and one-sided alpha 0.05, yet the trial is universally cited as showing drainage causes harm. Converting a noninferiority design into a superiority claim post hoc, even with a nominal superiority test appended, inflates confidence in the direction of effect","The trial is a pancreatic-head trial: 92% had adenocarcinoma and site was recorded only as 'pancreatic versus periampullary' as a covariate, with no subgroup result for ampullary tumours. Ampullary cancers are typically diagnosed at lower bilirubin, are more often endoscopically accessible and are far more often resectable, so the applicability of these complication rates to ampullary disease is assumed rather than shown","Only 61% of patients ultimately had a resection and 31% had palliative bypass; the palliative subgroup showed the largest difference (55% vs 18%, p = 0.003), so the headline result is partly driven by patients who were never going to benefit from resection and in whom stenting would now be definitive therapy rather than preoperative preparation","No blinding was possible for patients or surgeons, and the primary outcome - a complication 'that prompted an additional intervention resulting in extension of stay, readmission or death' - is partly a healthcare-utilisation endpoint sensitive to unblinded clinician behaviour, even though an adjudication committee classified events blind","Baseline imbalance in sex (70% vs 52% male, p = 0.01) and BMI (24.0 vs 25.2, p = 0.03) occurred despite randomisation and is handled only by covariate adjustment","Mortality was 7% overall and did not differ between arms, but the trial had no power for this: the relative risk for death from a protocol complication was 0.48 with an interval from 0.15 to 1.51","Events were counted to 120 days after randomisation, which in the drainage arm includes a 4-6 week pre-surgical window with no equivalent exposure period in the early surgery arm - so the drainage group was observed at risk for longer before the operation, which mechanically favours early surgery on a time-unadjusted count","A 2003-2008 trial predates routine metal stenting, modern ERCP prophylaxis including rectal NSAIDs and current neoadjuvant pathways; the authors' own recommendation at the end of the paper effectively concedes that the intervention tested is no longer the intervention used"],"n":"202 randomised, 196 analysed (94 early surgery, 102 preoperative biliary drainage) after 6 exclusions (2 withdrew consent, 4 ineligible bilirubin); resection performed in 63 (67%) versus 57 (56%), p = 0.11","bottom_line":"Routine 4-6 week preoperative plastic-stent biliary drainage before resection for pancreatic head cancer roughly doubles overall serious complications (74% vs 39%) because of stent-related cholangitis and occlusion, without reducing surgery-related complications or mortality - so early surgery is preferred when it can be arranged; the trial says nothing specific about ampullary tumours, used only plastic stents, and its null secondary result on surgical complications is the finding most often overlooked.","funding":"Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development, which had no access to outcome data during the trial and no role in analysis or manuscript preparation; no endoscopic equipment or stents were donated by manufacturers. Two authors disclosed lecture or consulting fees (Boston Scientific; GI Dynamics, Covidien, Johnson & Johnson)."},"22782416":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The unadjusted primary analysis did not show a significant benefit for adjuvant chemotherapy, and the authors state explicitly that the positive multivariable result and the gemcitabine-specific result should be considered hypothesis generating","A separate survival analysis for each tumour type could not be built into the trial design because the low incidence of each would have required an unattainably large sample and timeline; the different types were combined pragmatically because presentation and surgery are the same","Intrapancreatic bile duct cancer may need to be treated as a completely separate entity, and grouping should perhaps be avoided not only for ampullary but also for more proximal bile duct cancers","There was no single central review of histological sections - only central review of pathology reports by several experienced pathologists, which the authors argue makes systematic error unlikely","The dichotomised intestinal/pancreatobiliary classification was not widely applied when the trial started","Postoperative CA19-9 had too many missing values to be retained in the final models","The survival effect of chemotherapy was modest, indicating a need for further improvement and for testing combination chemotherapy"],"critique":["The adjustment that converts the result from negative to positive was for age, bile duct histology, poor differentiation and node positivity - and the observation arm was prognostically the worst on two of those at baseline (poorly differentiated 33% vs 22% and 19%; node positive 62% vs 60% and 54%), so the shift from HR 0.86 to 0.75 is partly correcting a randomisation imbalance. That cuts both ways, but it means the 0.75 is not an independent confirmation of the primary analysis; it is the same data with the imbalance removed, and its CI (0.57-0.98) only just excludes 1","The trial was powered on 243 deaths and 430 patients to detect a 12% absolute 5-year gain (HR 0.68) across the pooled periampullary population. It was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and it is the ampullary subgroup that pathway documents cite. With 297 ampullary patients, 151 deaths and three arms, no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival is reported at all - the ampullary medians of 40.6/57.8/70.8 months appear without a p value","Pooling created a group in which chemotherapy appeared harmful: in the 96 bile duct patients both regimens had numerically shorter median survival than observation. Any pooled 'benefit' is therefore driven entirely by the ampullary and other patients, and the trial's own discussion concedes bile duct cancer may be a separate entity - which is an argument that the pooled primary analysis answered the wrong question","The subtype analysis that the field quotes as evidence that subtype does not predict chemotherapy response is grossly underpowered: 162 of 297 ampullary tumours (55%) were indeterminate, leaving 80 intestinal and 46 pancreatobiliary split across three treatment arms - roughly 15-27 patients per subtype-by-arm cell. No interaction test, no numbers per cell and no power calculation are given, and 'tests of heterogeneity within pathological subgroups did not reveal any significant findings' is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence","Subtype was assigned from central review of pathology reports, not of slides; the same institutional tradition that produced these categories has since shown that slide-based subtyping has only fair reproducibility and that 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed, so 55% indeterminate is unsurprising and the 135 classified cases are a non-random, more clear-cut subset","Overall survival and disease-free survival point in opposite directions by subtype (pancreatobiliary numerically longer OS but significantly shorter DFS), which is biologically incoherent and suggests differential post-recurrence treatment or informative censoring rather than a true subtype effect in either direction","Disease-free survival is positive for both regimens on adjusted Cox analysis (HR 0.69 and 0.68, both p = 0.02) while unadjusted DFS is flatly negative (p = 0.48), the same adjusted/unadjusted divergence as the primary endpoint - consistent with the adjustment carrying the result throughout","Delivery was poor: a fifth of the fluorouracil arm never received a dose, half of each chemotherapy arm did not complete six cycles, and median dose intensity was 78% and 88% of protocol. An intention-to-treat null result under that much non-receipt is uninformative about efficacy, and the authors do not report a per-protocol or dose-intensity sensitivity analysis","Screening data on how many patients were excluded and why were not collected routinely, so the degree of selection into the trial is unknown","Median survival of 35 months in the untreated observation arm is far better than the ampullary literature of the era, implying a fit, early-stage, highly selected population; the absolute benefit of adjuvant therapy in a frailer, node-positive clinic population cannot be read off this trial","Five patients randomised to gemcitabine were excluded post-randomisation as ineligible (3 metastatic, 2 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) along with 1 in observation, a small departure from strict intention-to-treat that moves in the direction of the treatment arms"],"n":"434 randomised, 428 in the primary analysis (144 observation, 143 fluorouracil plus folinic acid, 141 gemcitabine); 297 ampullary, 96 intrapancreatic bile duct, 35 other (10 duodenal, 25 nondescript); 244 deaths (57%) at analysis","bottom_line":"The only randomised trial of adjuvant chemotherapy in resected periampullary cancer was negative on its primary endpoint (HR 0.86, p = 0.25) and became positive only in a prespecified multivariable analysis adjusting for age, bile duct histology, grade and nodal status (HR 0.75, p = 0.03) that the authors themselves call hypothesis generating; it establishes neither a benefit specific to ampullary cancer - the ampullary subgroup was never powered or formally tested - nor that intestinal and pancreatobiliary subtypes respond differently, since only 135 of 297 ampullary tumours could be subtyped at all.","funding":"Cancer Research United Kingdom; National Cancer Institute of Canada and Canadian Cancer Society; Fonds de Recherche de la Societe Nationale Francaise de Gastroenterologie; Fondazione Italiana Malattie del Pancreas; Health and Medical Research Council of Australia and state Cancer Councils; Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group. JPN part funded by the Liverpool NIHR Pancreas Biomedical Research Unit; MM part funded by the Oxford NIHR Biomedical Research Centre. Sponsors stated to have had no role in design, conduct, analysis or manuscript. No author conflicts of interest reported."},"23026934":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["No limitations section; the authors concede only that the ampullary-NOS category doubles as a waste-basket for cases that cannot be confidently assigned, and that whether the intra-ampullary group's survival advantage reflects small invasion size or a genuinely different biology is unknown","They acknowledge the periampullary-duodenal versus duodenal carcinoma survival comparison failed to reach significance because of small numbers"],"critique":["The four categories were assigned retrospectively from archived gross descriptions and slides by the same authors who devised the scheme - no blinded or independent reassignment, and no interobserver agreement statistic, so the reproducibility of the gross algorithm that the whole classification rests on is untested here","The periampullary-duodenal group that anchors the favourable-prognosis claim has only 12 patients, 6 of them node positive; the survival estimates carry no confidence intervals anywhere in the paper and no multivariable model adjusting for T stage, node status or invasion size is reported despite a Cox model being described in the methods","Invasion size - the variable that drives the survival ordering - was in part estimated by applying an invasive/non-invasive ratio read off slides to the gross size, i.e. derived rather than measured, which biases exactly the comparison between the preinvasive-rich (intra-ampullary) and preinvasive-poor (ampullary-ductal) groups","Comparators are convenience cohorts from the same archives (113 PDAC, 55 duodenal) with no matching for stage, size, node status or treatment, and adjuvant therapy is not recorded at all, so the headline 'ampullary carcinoma is distinct from PDAC' survival gap conflates stage migration and resectability with biology","Follow-up was partly obtained from SEER and by telephoning treating physicians, with cases carrying missing values excluded variable by variable, so denominators shift between tables without being stated","Reclassifying 21% of cases out of the ampullary category inevitably removes the worst-prognosis tumours (mostly pancreatic) from the ampullary group, which mechanically improves ampullary survival relative to the historical literature - a definitional effect the paper presents as a biological finding"],"n":"249 strictly defined ampullary carcinomas culled from 1469 malignant pancreatoduodenectomy specimens, compared with 113 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas and 55 non-ampullary duodenal carcinomas","bottom_line":"Establishes a reproducible-in-principle anatomic definition of ampullary carcinoma and shows that four gross/microscopic site-specific subsets differ markedly in stage and outcome, but the prognostic separation rests on small, unadjusted, single-reader subgroups and does not establish the classification's reproducibility or independence from stage.","funding":"Supported in part by the Georgia Cancer Coalition Distinguished Cancer Clinicians and Scientists Program; authors declare no financial interest in any commercial company pertaining to the article"},"25293823":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design with no predefined criteria for proceeding from EUS to endoscopic or surgical resection, which may have produced inconsistent surgical referral and influenced endoscopic outcomes","The exact length of intraductal extension was not documented (only that it ranged from subcentimetre to about 1 cm)","The data represent only the subset of ampullary tumours at the institution that had EUS, since some patients went directly to ERCP"],"critique":["The reference standard is circular for the lesions that matter most: for endoscopically resected adenomas, absence of intraductal extension was assumed whenever resection was complete with a negative margin and cholangiography showed no ductal extension - so EUS is being validated partly against a composite that already includes EUS-era endoscopic judgement, which inflates specificity and accuracy","The two comparisons use different denominators (90, 102 and 81 patients) drawn from the same cohort by availability of ERCP or of a resection specimen, so the claim that EUS and ERCP 'perform similarly' compares non-overlapping subsets rather than paired readings in the same patients","Sensitivity rests on very few events: 9-12 patients with intraductal extension in each analysis, which is why the AUROC confidence intervals are wide and why the EUS-versus-ERCP difference cannot be resolved","The 90% T-staging accuracy is carried almost entirely by correctly calling 65 of 66 lesions confined to the ampulla; for the invasive categories that would actually change management, accuracy was 78-80% and EUS systematically understaged","Six endosonographers and six ERCP endoscopists over 15 years, with no blinding, no central re-reading and no interobserver data; the authors concede EUS is operator dependent and that their results may reflect high-volume performance, which limits transfer to community practice","The 91% complete-resection rate is presented as evidence that EUS triaged patients well, but it is a before-after comparison with the same group's earlier 73% series and could equally reflect cohort selection, era effects or stricter criteria; patients deemed unresectable at EUS were excluded from that earlier study, making the two rates non-comparable","A 1998-2012 accrual spans radial and linear instruments and major changes in echoendoscope technology (GF-UM20 through GF-UC140P), and the radial/linear comparison is reported on 75 versus 21 patients without a formal test","The 17% non-adenomatous rate on papillectomy is a striking finding about referral biopsy reliability, but it also means the cohort's composition - and therefore every accuracy estimate - depends on outside histology that the centre did not verify"],"n":"119 patients undergoing EUS for an ampullary lesion (99 with adenoma or adenocarcinoma); ERCP in 90; surgical pathology available for 102 (EUS comparison) and 81 (ERCP comparison); 58 underwent endoscopic papillectomy","bottom_line":"In expert hands and with no biliary stent in place, EUS stages ampullary lesions about as well as ERCP against surgical pathology and is excellent at confirming T1 disease, but it misses roughly a fifth of intraductal extensions and a fifth of deeper invasion, and this retrospective design with a partly circular reference standard cannot show that adding EUS improves resection outcomes.","funding":"None stated; all authors disclosed no relevant financial relationships"},"2571019":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["No limitations section. The authors note that the retrospective series yielded fewer polyps with fewer biopsies and attribute between-centre variation in reported prevalence (28% to 100%) to the same technical differences","They state that upper gastrointestinal cancer develops slowly in FAP, with a median interval of 22 years after colectomy in a cited series of 37 patients, so natural history was not observed in this study","They acknowledge that the natural history of these polyps is largely unknown, which is why the mortality of prophylactic pancreatoduodenectomy must be weighed against it, and that endoscopic removal is often impractical while photodynamic therapy and vitamin C chemoprevention are unproven"],"critique":["THE STAGING SYSTEM THAT THIS LITERATURE STILL USES WAS NEVER VALIDATED HERE. It was devised from a single cross-sectional screening round, with the four components and their cut-points assigned by the authors on the basis of 'known adenoma/cancer risk factors' rather than derived from or tested against any cancer outcome. No patient in this paper developed duodenal cancer during the study, so the association between stage IV and malignancy is asserted, not measured - and the four subsequent decades have never produced a formal validation, as the Mavani paper in this depot notes","The score has no weighting rationale: polyp number, size, histology and dysplasia each contribute 1-3 points as though equally important, and the stage boundaries (0, 1-4, 5-6, 7-8, 9-12) are arbitrary breaks in a 4-12 point range. Later work in this depot shows large polyp size rather than polyp number carries the cancer risk, and that the score omits the papilla entirely despite this very paper showing that is where the disease concentrates","The paper's own strongest finding - that the papilla is twice as likely to be adenomatous as the surrounding duodenum and that periampullary biopsy found adenoma in 11 patients with an otherwise normal duodenum - is not incorporated into the score that the paper proposes, an internal inconsistency that took until the 2019 ESGE guideline to correct","Because the score requires histology for two of its four components, it mandates biopsy of duodenal polyps and the papilla; ampullary biopsy is now known to cause pancreatitis and to produce fibrosis that compromises later endoscopic resection, so the system creates a harm that current guidelines explicitly try to avoid","47 of the 102 prospective patients also contribute to the retrospective series, so the prospective-versus-retrospective yield comparison is a within-patient comparison of two eras presented alongside a between-series comparison, and the 190-540% increases conflate better instruments, a single experienced endoscopist, and more biopsies without separating them","Everything is cross-sectional: 'stage IV occurred more often in the elderly' is a prevalence observation across ages, not progression, and cannot distinguish disease progression from cohort effects or ascertainment","No interobserver or intraobserver reproducibility data for polyp counting, size estimation or dysplasia grading, the four inputs to the score. Two of the ongoing studies the Soons review lists, three decades later, are still trying to establish exactly this","The mortality comparison used to motivate the programme (9 upper GI versus 4 rectal cancer deaths) comes from a separate 1948-1987 cohort of 197 patients with no denominators by follow-up time and no competing-risk accounting, in an era when colectomy practice and rectal surveillance differed entirely from the screened population","The bile-exposure hypothesis for the distal duodenal and periampullary distribution is offered with experimental and epidemiological citations but no measurement in these patients, and the search for a bile tumour promoter it launched has not succeeded","The surveillance intervals recommended (3 years for mild/moderate, at least yearly for stage IV) are stated without any analysis of interval cancers, cost or patient burden, and remain substantially the intervals in use today","The text extraction for this paper is incomplete and damaged: the 'Severity of duodenal polyposis' table - which carried the number of patients per stage and the mean polyp measurements - renders as an empty stub, and the file continues into an unrelated Lancet article on cell-surface peptidases, so the per-stage distribution beyond the 11 stage IV patients cannot be verified from this source"],"n":"102 patients screened prospectively (69 families, 59 men, 43 women, mean age 41 years, range 14-66); retrospective series 94 patients with 163 endoscopies (61 families, mean age at first endoscopy 39 years, range 15-73), of whom 47 overlapped with the prospective study","bottom_line":"The paper that established that duodenal and periampullary adenomas are near-universal in FAP, concentrate on the papilla, and have displaced colorectal cancer as a cause of death - and that introduced the Spigelman stage still used to set surveillance intervals; but the score was constructed by expert judgement from a single cross-sectional screening round with no cancer outcomes, has never been formally validated, and conspicuously omits the ampulla that the same paper identified as the highest-risk site.","funding":"ADS supported by the St Mark's Research Foundation; the Imperial Cancer Research Fund enabled purchase of the side-viewing video-endoscope for the St Mark's endoscopy unit"},"25783680":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective and multi-institutional, so the gross dissection and node-sampling method was not standardised across centres","Data on adjuvant therapy were not available","Retrospective design can establish association only, not causation"],"critique":["The missing adjuvant-therapy data are not a minor gap: node-positive patients are precisely the ones most likely to have received chemotherapy, so the N1/N2 hazard ratios are confounded by treatment in an unknown direction","The cut-points were not derived here - they were imported from Kang's SEER analysis - yet no attempt is made to test alternative thresholds (the paper's own Table 3 lists published cut-offs of 2, 3 and 4 nodes), so this is a single-threshold confirmation rather than a validation of the optimal threshold","Node yield varied from 1 to 61, and 52% of cases had fewer than 12 nodes; understaging in that half inflates the apparent N0 survival, which is the comparison that makes substaging look useful. The authors note the N0 and N1 curves overlap once sampling is adequate but still recommend the scheme, and the implication - that N1 may carry little prognostic weight over N0 when staging is done properly - is left unresolved rather than treated as a finding against the proposal","N2 cases were markedly over-represented at the one institution using the orange-peeling dissection method (26% vs 13.5% elsewhere), so the N1/N2 split is partly a marker of which pathology lab handled the specimen","Half the cohort was alive at analysis (155/308) with median follow-up only 56 months, so the 5-year estimates for N1 and N2 (31.5% and 30%, essentially identical) rest on few events and offer no separation at the time point clinicians use","No competing-risk analysis in a cohort with mean age 64 and median survival approaching 9 years in the N0 group, where non-cancer death is a substantial competing event","Interobserver agreement on the ampullary-origin determination by the five reviewers is not reported, although the same group showed elsewhere that related ampullary classifications are only fairly reproducible"],"n":"313 invasive ampullary carcinomas; 142 (45%) node positive; median 11 nodes examined (range 1-61); 150 (48%) had 12 or more nodes examined","bottom_line":"Shows in a pathologically verified cohort that the number of metastatic nodes stratifies survival in ampullary carcinoma and supports adding an N1/N2 split to TNM, but the effect is modest, unadjusted for adjuvant therapy, and the N0-versus-N1 distinction largely disappears once at least 12 nodes are examined.","funding":"None stated; authors declare no affiliation with or financial involvement in any organisation with a financial interest in the subject matter"},"26479271":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["Small sample size: this was explicitly a pilot study with no prospective power calculation, and an adequately powered study is needed to compare pancreatitis rates between the two methods","Risk factors for post-procedural pancreatitis were not investigated and may have confounded the results","The authors state they cannot conclude that recurrence was higher in the conventional group because that group included three patients with cancer whereas the wire-guided group had none"],"critique":["A pilot study with no power calculation and 7 events across 45 patients cannot exclude a clinically important difference in either direction; because an uptick in recurrence may occur after 4 years and not all patients were followed that long, the results may underestimate the true recurrence rate","Given the low number of recurrences, identification of risk factors was underpowered","All procedures were performed by endoscopists with substantial ERCP experience, and papillectomy carries an ASGE level 4 complexity rating, further limiting generalisability"],"critique":["The internal arithmetic does not add up: the abstract reports 20 recurrences, but the en bloc versus piecemeal breakdown gives 13 plus 4 (17), and the complete versus residual breakdown gives 15 plus 2 (17). Three recurrences are unaccounted for in both stratifications, so the denominators behind the comparisons cannot be verified","The paper's central claim about timing is stated two different ways: the abstract says 9 of 20 recurrences (45%) occurred after the first 2 years of surveillance, while the discussion says 'nearly half the recurrences occurred after 3 years of surveillance' and that the probability of recurrence 'experienced a leap 4 years after papillectomy'. The Kaplan-Meier table shows no events in year 4 at all, so the narrative does not match the data","Recurrence counts by resection type run counter to every other series and to the paper's own framing: 19.4% after en bloc versus 7.0% after piecemeal resection, and 16.5% after initially complete versus 6.1% after residual-tissue resection. These are reported without comment, but they are the signature of detection bias - patients with piecemeal or residual disease were scoped more intensively early, had their lesions re-treated, and so were classified as residual rather than recurrent","That classification is the deeper problem: by requiring one negative surveillance endoscopy before an event counts as recurrence, and by allowing multiple treatment sessions within 'complete eradication', the study converts early incomplete resection into non-events and shifts the apparent recurrence curve rightwards - which is precisely the direction needed to argue for longer surveillance","With 20 events and 13 candidate variables, the Cox model is severely overfitted; every adjusted hazard ratio is below 1.4 with intervals spanning 0.1 to 7.7, so the finding that 'no variables predicted recurrence' is uninformative rather than reassuring, as the authors concede","Mean follow-up of 2.8 years against a mean time to recurrence of 3.2 years means more than half the person-time needed to observe the events being described was never accumulated; the 5-year cumulative estimate of 14.5% rests on a thin tail, and the recommendation to extend surveillance to 10 years is driven by a single outlier recurrence at 9.75 years","The 18-year accrual window spans the introduction of high-definition endoscopy, narrow band imaging, radiofrequency ablation and routine rectal NSAIDs (given to only 26.5% of this cohort), so technique, detection sensitivity and complication risk all changed within the cohort, and no era analysis is presented","21 patients with adenocarcinoma are pooled into an adenoma recurrence series; only 12 of them entered the recurrence analysis, and 2 recurred with adenocarcinoma - events with entirely different clinical meaning from an adenoma recurrence, counted in the same rate","The FAP comparison that contradicts the much-cited 58% recurrence figure from Ma et al. is based on 35 FAP patients with a shorter follow-up than that study, and the authors acknowledge this, yet the abstract-level message ('recurrence rate did not differ by baseline pathology') invites readers to drop FAP-specific surveillance","Adverse events of 27.2% including 4.8% perforation and 2.2% severe pancreatitis are higher than in most comparator series in this depot, but are reported without any analysis of predictors or era, and are not weighed against the recurrence findings in the conclusion","Follow-up data were supplemented by telephone calls to patients, an ascertainment method that cannot confirm histological recurrence and introduces differential completeness between patients still attending the centre and those lost to it","Several authors declare consultancies with endoscope and device manufacturers (Boston Scientific, Olympus, Cook, Medtronic) in a paper whose conclusion is to extend endoscopic surveillance to 10 years"],"n":"165 papillectomies screened, 136 patients with adenomatous pathology analysed (mean age 61.9, SD 15; 70 women, 51.5%; mean lesion size 21.2 mm, SD 12); 124 (91.2%) achieved complete eradication and entered the recurrence analysis with 345.8 person-years of follow-up (mean 2.8 years per patient, SD 3.3)","bottom_line":"Reports a 16.1% recurrence rate (5.8 per 100 person-years) after endoscopic papillectomy with recurrences occurring as late as 9.75 years and roughly half after the recommended 2-year surveillance window, which supports longer follow-up; but the event counts are internally inconsistent, the mean follow-up (2.8 years) is shorter than the mean time to recurrence (3.2 years), and the counter-intuitive finding of more recurrence after en bloc and after initially complete resection points to detection bias in how residual disease was classified.","funding":"NIH T32DK007038 (SH). Multiple author disclosures: advisory board membership and consultancies with Boston Scientific, Olympus, Cook Medical, Medtronic, Cernostics, Exact Sciences and Interpace, and research funding from Lucid, Ambu and CDx."},"39642968":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design in which selection bias and missing data cannot be definitively excluded, mitigated by requiring consecutive inclusion and by the matched analysis","No formal study monitoring was possible because of limited resources, and monitoring of cases not included during the study period was not possible","Both low- and high-volume centres were included and centre volume was not analysed, which the authors defend as better reflecting daily practice","Excluding patients with missing data could itself introduce selection bias, although an exclusion analysis showed those patients were comparable on age, sex, comorbidities and lesion size","Recurrence can only be reliably excluded by careful endoscopy with routine biopsy even when macroscopy is normal, and such detailed data are not available in a large retrospective database, so later recurrences cannot be excluded","The reported 16% recurrence after histologic R0 means complete resection should be interpreted with caution","Submucosal injection, used in 24.2% of matched papillectomy patients, is no longer recommended by ESGE but was permitted by the original database criteria and could have influenced the endoscopic results","The study was not designed to analyse survival","Lesions beyond 30 mm could not be evaluated because too few were available in the matched cohorts","A randomised trial would give the highest level of evidence but is judged unrealistic: a two-armed trial would need 190 randomised patients (95 per group, alpha 0.05, power 0.95, effect size 0.5) and with an estimated 30% dropout a screening population of 315 patients with ampullary lesions, and surgical ampullectomy is not broadly available"],"critique":["The matched comparison is almost entirely one-sided in construction: the 62 matched pairs represent 98.4% of the eligible surgical patients but only 10.9% of the eligible papillectomy patients, so the surgical arm is its whole population while the endoscopic arm is a 1-in-9 selection chosen to resemble it. Any residual difference in the matched analysis reflects which papillectomy patients could be matched, not a balanced contrast","Matching omitted the variables that most obviously drove the choice of procedure and the chance of R0: intraductal extension, bile and pancreatic duct dilation, and the use of concomitant ablation (patients ablated at the index papillectomy were deliberately excluded from matching). Table 4 shows intrabiliary extension on imaging and duct dilation still differed significantly after matching (21% vs 8.1%, p = 0.01; 45.2% vs 30.6%, p = 0.001), so confounding by indication survives the propensity model","Follow-up was more than twice as long in the surgical arm in both cohorts (37.5 vs 15.5 months after matching), which biases the recurrence comparison - the paper's clearest finding - against the endoscopic arm's apparent advantage and in favour of the surgical arm's 3.2%; a recurrence rate cannot be compared between arms observed for different durations without a time-to-event analysis, and none is presented for recurrence","Conversely, surveillance intensity was asymmetric in the other direction: endoscopic patients were routinely scoped with biopsies of the scar while surgical patients were not systematically re-scoped, so the fivefold recurrence difference conflates true residual disease with differential ascertainment. The authors acknowledge recurrence 'much depends on the scrutiny of follow-up' but still attribute the difference to the deeper resection plane of ampullectomy","The surgical arm has 63 patients and 6 cancers. Every surgical subgroup statement - 66.6% R0 in cancer (4 of 6), 92.9% R0 in adenoma (53 of 57), 3.2% recurrence (2 of 63) - rests on single-digit numerators, and the only procedure-related death also sits in that arm, so the safety comparison (1.9% vs 3.2%, p = 0.38) has no power at all to detect the morbidity difference that drives the clinical choice","23.2% of the 1673 eligible datasets were excluded for missing or inconclusive data and a further 652 for clinical reasons, leaving 40% of papillectomies and 25% of ampullectomies. The exclusion analysis compares only age, sex, comorbidities and lesion size - not stage, margin or outcome - so it cannot rule out that outcome-related data were differentially missing","The R0 definition is applied to specimens handled by local pathologists at 58 centres over 14 years with no central review, no interobserver assessment and no standard protocol; given that the adjacent literature shows 26% of en bloc papillectomy specimens cannot even be margin-assessed, R0 is being compared between a fragmented endoscopic specimen and an intact surgical one, which structurally favours surgery independent of oncological completeness","Attributing additional ablation at the index procedure to presumed visible residual tissue and therefore reclassifying it as R2 is a reasonable assumption, but it is an assumption made retrospectively by the authors; the 65.9% figure that results is then used as the real papillectomy success rate, and both 80.2% and 65.9% appear in the paper without a single preferred estimate","T1a and T1b cancers are pooled in most analyses despite the authors noting these carry significantly different nodal metastasis risk, and the 13 T1b patients treated endoscopically are precisely the group in whom local resection is most questionable","The matched-cohort severe complication counts are 1 versus 2 events, yet the paper concludes 'both procedures were safe'; with these numbers a two- or threefold difference in serious morbidity would be undetectable","Overall survival is reported as comparable in a study the authors concede was not designed to analyse survival, with median follow-up 21 months in a disease whose resected median survival exceeds 4 years - the survival curves carry essentially no information and should not be used to support equivalence","Procedures spanning 2007-2020 include the pre-ESGE-guideline era, submucosal injection in a quarter of matched endoscopic cases, and the introduction of endobiliary radiofrequency ablation; no era stratification is performed despite technique having changed materially"],"n":"From 2862 patients in the ESAP database (1189 pancreatoduodenectomies excluded first), 1673 remained (1422 papillectomy, 251 surgical ampullectomy); after exclusions 569 papillectomy (40.0% of database papillectomies) and 63 surgical ampullectomy (25.1%) were analysed, with 62 matched pairs; median follow-up 21 months (IQR 10-47)","bottom_line":"The largest comparison of endoscopic papillectomy with transduodenal surgical ampullectomy shows that a third of procedures in both arms were done for the wrong indication (non-neoplastic histology or advanced cancer), that surgery achieves higher initial R0 (90% vs 73%) with far lower recurrence after R0 (3.2% vs 16%) but at 7 times the procedure time and 11 extra hospital days, and that papillectomy fails in two-thirds of T1 cancers; but the matched analysis pairs the entire surgical population with a 1-in-9 selection of endoscopic patients, follow-up was twice as long in the surgical arm, and surveillance intensity differed, so the recurrence gap is inflated by design.","funding":"The authors have not declared a specific grant for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors. Multiple author disclosures including honoraria from FUJIFILM and Falk Foundation and institutional consultancies with Boston Scientific, Cook Medical and Pentax Medical. Ethics approval from the University of Leipzig (455/18-ek)."},"39831703":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective multi-institutional data with the usual biases; overall statistical power remained low because of disease rarity despite multiple centres","The small sample prevented splitting into derivation and validation cohorts, so the proposed score has not undergone formal validation","Ampullary lesions were not separated from duodenal lesions involving the periampullary region, although no outcome difference was found between them","Not every patient was tested genetically for FAP, MUTYH-associated polyposis or other mutations, though all underwent colonoscopy and family history assessment","Sampling bias is acknowledged because the cohort consists only of non-FAP periampullary adenomas that went on to pancreatoduodenectomy; the high malignancy rate reflects selection of high-risk cases by tumour size and location, and the true denominator - including patients managed by endoscopic mucosal resection or transduodenal resection - is unclear","A prospective study to identify the true denominator may not be feasible given the low incidence"],"critique":["The three risk strata are reported with mutually inconsistent numbers: the abstract gives low risk n = 26, intermediate n = 59, high n = 26 with rates 10.3%, 44.1% and 88.2%; the results text gives 11.5%, 41.7% and 84.6%; Table 4 gives 3/29, 26/59 and 30/34. Three different sets of denominators for the paper's central output means the score's calibration cannot be verified from the published data","The score was derived and evaluated in the same 127 patients with no split-sample, bootstrap or cross-validation, no c-statistic, no calibration plot and no sensitivity or specificity at any threshold. An OR of 77.5 for the high-risk group (CI 15.9-375.9) is the signature of an in-sample fit, and the paper's own concession that validation was impossible should preclude clinical use","The denominator problem the authors acknowledge is fatal to the score's intended purpose: everyone in the cohort had a Whipple, so the score is calibrated on the subset already judged to need resection. A patient weighing resection against endoscopic surveillance is by definition outside this population, and applying a 46% baseline malignancy rate to them would badly overestimate risk - exactly the misuse the shared-decision framing invites","Two of the four score components are proxies for obstruction, not for neoplastic progression: 'any preoperative symptom' (worth 2 points) is a list including fatigue, nausea and dark urine, and common bile duct dilation of 9 mm or more. Jaundice and biliary stenting were dropped from the model as redundant with symptoms, which concedes the point - the score largely measures whether the lesion is obstructing, and the discussant at the meeting objected that a jaundiced patient with no other factor scores only 1-2","The inverse complication relationship is presented as a feature of the score but has a simpler explanation the paper does not address: patients with benign pathology had soft, non-atrophic glands and non-dilated ducts because they had no obstructing cancer, and fistula risk follows gland texture and duct size. Adjusting for duct size and texture in the final model does not remove this, because the same obstruction physiology that lowers fistula risk is what the score is detecting","The complication finding only becomes significant after the three prespecified strata are collapsed at score 3 - across the strata as defined it was non-significant (p = 0.11) with the intermediate and high groups indistinguishable (27.1% vs 29.4%). Choosing the dichotomy that yields p = 0.047 after the three-group comparison failed is a post hoc cut-point","Preoperative dysplasia grade carries 2 of the 6 points but was read by local pathologists at 8 centres over 12 years, with no central review and no interobserver data - and the invited discussants specifically questioned whether a pathologist seeing roughly one such case per year can reliably separate high- from low-grade dysplasia","Volume was extremely low: 127 patients across 8 institutions over 12 years, about 1.3 cases per centre per year, so biopsy technique, number of biopsies, prior attempted endoscopic resection and pathology interpretation almost certainly varied in ways that cannot be modelled - a point the discussants raised and the authors do not rebut with data","EUS findings are absent from the entire paper despite both discussants noting that these are major centres where EUS would be routine; omitting the modality that best assesses intraductal extension and depth from a preoperative risk score is a substantial gap, and no explanation is given","Lesion size was missing for 27 of 127 patients (21%) and was then excluded from the score on the grounds that it did not differ between groups - a conclusion drawn from data with a fifth missing and no imputation","Black race was associated with benign final pathology (26.5% vs 11.9%) and with a different risk profile, in a cohort where race also tracked with symptoms and stenting; no analysis addresses whether differential access to earlier endoscopic diagnosis is embedded in the score's components","The 46.4% malignancy rate is compared with the same group's earlier single-centre figure of 29%, with no explanation for the difference other than cohort composition - which again points to the selection the score cannot escape"],"n":"127 patients of 189 reviewed; median age 65 years (34-89), 57 men (44.9%); 82 (64.6%) preoperative duodenal adenoma and 45 (35.4%) ampullary adenoma, with ampullary involvement in 84 of 119 (70.6%); 59 (46.4%) had malignancy on final pathology","bottom_line":"Confirms in the largest surgical series that nearly half of sporadic periampullary adenomas taken to pancreatoduodenectomy harbour cancer and that patients with benign final pathology paradoxically suffer threefold more major complications, and proposes a 0-6 malignancy risk score from age, bile duct diameter, symptoms and high-grade dysplasia; but the score is derived and tested in the same 127 already-resected patients with no validation, its published strata carry three inconsistent sets of numbers, and two of its four components are proxies for biliary obstruction.","funding":"National Cancer Institute of the NIH award K12 CA237806 (Emory K12 Clinical Oncology Training Program, Dr Shah); Contardi Research Fellowship; Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Awards UL1 TR002378. Nothing to disclose for the study; disclosures outside its scope include grant funding from Cantargia AB and consultancies with Intera Oncology, Stryker Medical and Intuitive Surgical."},"40729532":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The Delphi methodology, while the best option for reaching consensus, carries the difficulty of capturing all key issues in the literature during questionnaire development, depends on panellists' ongoing willingness to participate, and risks skewed data because those less confident about a topic may not participate","Although the stated aim was to cover all non-pancreatic cancers of the periampullary region, more recommendations relate to ampullary cancer than to common bile duct or duodenal cancer; the authors accept this imbalance as reflecting greater uncertainty and need for guidance about ampullary cancer","For a considerable proportion of the consensus questions there are fairly limited published data, so most recommendations are supported only by a low level of evidence, which the authors say highlights the early stage of knowledge about periampullary cancer","The authors state that the lack of consensus definitions and standardisation, together with high interobserver variability, has hindered consistent conclusions across studies - particularly regarding patient management including the efficacy of adjuvant chemotherapy, which remains highly controversial because of these inconsistencies"],"critique":["Almost every recommendation is graded low level of evidence with a weak form of recommendation, or rests on expert opinion alone. This is honest, but it means a document that will be used to standardise reporting worldwide is in substance a codification of the opinions of 43 experts, most of them from the pathology study groups that initiated it","THE PROCESS METRICS PROMISED ARE NOT REPORTED. The methods describe an independent Jury Committee calculating a 'Quality Score' using the AGREE II tool across 23 items and six domains, and an audience vote on each recommendation at the Brescia meeting. Neither result appears anywhere in the paper - no AGREE II score, no domain breakdown, no audience agreement percentages. The quality-assurance apparatus is described but its findings are withheld","The Delphi convergence is itself a weak signal: 33 of 57 recommendations reached 80% agreement in round one and the rest were revised by the responsible expert team according to the dissenting comments and re-voted until they passed. Revising a statement until it achieves consensus guarantees consensus; the final 50 of 51 figure measures iteration, not agreement on the original propositions","The 30% threshold for calling a tumour 'mixed' subtype has no stated derivation. It is a cut-point that will determine subtype assignment in a large fraction of cases - and the consensus itself cites that about 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed - yet no data, reproducibility study or sensitivity analysis is offered for choosing 30% over 10% or 50%","Renaming the hybrid category 'tubular-NOS' is a nomenclature change, not a solution. The underlying problem documented in this depot - that five pathologists agree on morphological subtype at kappa 0.39 with full agreement in 23% of cases - is unaddressed: no interobserver reproducibility study of the new definitions is reported or planned, so the consensus standardises the words without demonstrating that the categories can be applied consistently","The consensus states plainly that the prognostic and predictive role of subtype is unclear because of inconsistent historical definitions, yet it simultaneously retains subtyping as a required element of the pathology report and advises subtyping on biopsy where subtype 'may affect treatment'. If subtype has no established treatment implication, there is no situation in which that condition is met","Reflex MMR testing is recommended on the grounds that prevalence is 'comparable to that of colorectal cancer and is also independent on the subtype', but the supporting evidence is graded low and the two papers in this depot give prevalences of 15% in unselected non-medullary ampullary carcinoma and 4.3% in early-onset ampullary cancer - neither of which is clearly comparable to colorectal, and neither of which is cited as a prevalence estimate in the recommendation","Tumour budding is recommended as prognostically stronger than T stage and nodal metastasis, a strong empirical claim resting largely on work from the same institutional tradition that produced the ampullary classifications, with no multi-institutional validation, no reproducibility data for the 3-foci-per-200x-field threshold, and the acknowledged problem that biopsies may not contain the invasive front where budding must be assessed","229 of 37061 screened articles (0.6%) were selected, with allocation of articles to anonymous expert teams but no stated inclusion criteria, no risk-of-bias appraisal of the 229, no PRISMA flow diagram in the main text and no evidence tables - so the SIGN framework is invoked without the apparatus that makes it auditable","The anatomic definitions, which are the document's most valuable contribution, are operationalised in terms of tumour 'epicentre' and 'minimal involvement' without quantitative thresholds except in the earlier Adsay scheme they derive from; given that this literature's own data show that 21% of cases labelled ampullary are reclassified on strict review, the definitions need a reproducibility study more than they need wider adoption","The panel is heavily weighted towards pathology (initiated by ISGACA with ISGPP as steering committee), and the multidisciplinary part generated only 17 of 51 recommendations; the oncological questions that clinicians most need settled - whether subtype should guide adjuvant therapy, what to do with a T1 cancer after papillectomy - are declared unresolved rather than addressed","The consensus correctly identifies that inconsistent definitions have made the adjuvant chemotherapy literature uninterpretable, which is the strongest argument in this depot against acting on the Bolm-versus-Ecker dispute; but it stops at saying standardised future studies are needed and offers no interim guidance"],"bottom_line":"The first international consensus to define precisely what counts as ampullary carcinoma, to retire the term 'periampullary' as a diagnosis, to set a 30% threshold for the mixed subtype and rename the hybrid group 'tubular-NOS', to make mismatch repair testing reflex, and to state explicitly that the prognostic and predictive value of intestinal-versus-pancreatobiliary subtype remains unclear because the historical literature used inconsistent definitions - which is the key caveat for any pathway claiming subtype should guide adjuvant therapy; but almost every recommendation is low-evidence or expert opinion, the promised AGREE II quality score and audience vote are never reported, and no reproducibility study accompanies the new definitions.","funding":"Amsterdam Gastroenterology Endocrinology Metabolism (AGEM), Amsterdam, The Netherlands; the authors declare no conflicts of interest"},"41192607":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design over a 10-year period across 22 institutions, which may introduce missing data and selection bias","Treatment strategies - papillectomy technique, surveillance intervals and argon plasma coagulation use - varied by institution and over time because standardised guidelines were not consistently available; the authors stratified analysis by treatment period to address this","Only high-volume centres with expert teams were included, limiting generalisability","R0 margin status was assessed locally at each institution rather than centrally, which may introduce variability, although recurrence rates after R0 were comparable to other large studies","T1a and T1b adenocarcinomas were not differentiated, so prognosis by tumour stage could not be examined"],"critique":["The hazard ratios differ between the abstract/discussion and Table 2 for the same comparisons (Rx 2.30 [1.44-3.68] versus 2.38 [1.49-3.81]; R1 2.95 [1.85-4.71] versus 2.95 [1.87-4.66]). The discrepancy is small but it means two different models or datasets were in play and neither is identified","The central finding - recurrence after R0 - is partly a definitional artefact of Japanese pathological practice, which the paper itself flags: non-invasive intraepithelial neoplasia is diagnosed as carcinoma in Japan but as high-grade dysplasia in the West, so 'adenocarcinoma' in the 92 cases here is not equivalent to adenocarcinoma in the Western series alongside it, and the adenocarcinoma hazard ratio cannot be transferred","Recurrence is defined as histologic confirmation of neoplastic tissue with no requirement for a prior negative surveillance endoscopy, and the median time to recurrence was 6 months (3 months after R1). That makes a large fraction of 'recurrences' residual disease, as the pattern by margin status shows - which is consistent but means the 18.3% figure is not comparable with series that excluded residual disease, including Han 2024 in this same depot","The later treatment era (2015-2020) independently predicted recurrence (HR 1.57), which the authors attribute to more procedures by operators with fewer than 20 prior cases (26.4% rising to 44.0%). Since operator experience was not itself significant, this is an unexplained period effect that could equally reflect intensified surveillance in later years - a detection artefact that would inflate the headline recurrence rate","Margin assessment was local across 22 centres with no central pathology review and no interobserver data, yet R0/R1/Rx is the paper's principal exposure; a quarter of the cohort was Rx precisely because margins could not be read, and Rx behaved almost identically to R1 at 5 years (34% each), suggesting Rx is largely undetected R1","The R0 subgroup analysis generates the paper's most quotable new risk factors from very few events, with wildly unstable estimates: argon plasma coagulation HR 6.26 (1.44-27.1) rests on 69 of 396 R0 patients having received APC, and bile duct invasion HR 4.86 (1.08-21.8) on a handful of cases. The authors correctly reinterpret APC as a marker of endoscopically suspected residual disease rather than a cause, but the abstract-level framing does not carry that caveat","The pancreatic duct invasion estimate is reported as 0.00 (0.00-infinity) - a non-estimate from a zero cell - and is then used to argue that bile duct but not pancreatic duct invasion matters, an inference the data cannot support","Patients censored at 5 years and 21 patients removed for post-papillectomy surgery for residual cancer are exactly the group at highest risk of a bad outcome; removing them from the recurrence denominator while keeping them in the 798-patient resection-status analysis means the two headline numbers (52.1% R0, 18.3% recurrence) have different populations behind them","Female sex emerged as an independent predictor in both models (HR 1.48 and 2.09) with no mechanism offered beyond one prior report; in a model with 13 covariates and 142 events this is as likely to be noise or a proxy for an unmeasured anatomical variable","Follow-up protocols 'varied by center and clinical context' with only a typical interval of 6-12 months stated, so recurrence ascertainment is non-uniform across 22 centres and 12 years - the single most important determinant of a cumulative recurrence estimate is left undocumented","The 32.5% adverse event rate with 19.4% bleeding is substantially higher than most Western series and reflects a Japanese practice of inpatient papillectomy with a 13-day median stay; the paper does not discuss whether this reflects more complete ascertainment or a different complication profile, which matters for anyone comparing the two approaches","Several authors declare lecture fees and research support from endoscope and device manufacturers, and the study was run with the national endoscopy society's guideline committee, in a paper whose conclusions support continued endoscopic surveillance and a redefinition of R0"],"n":"875 cases enrolled, 798 with pathologically confirmed ampullary adenoma or adenocarcinoma, 776 in the long-term recurrence analysis (21 excluded for surgery for confirmed or suspected residual adenocarcinoma, 1 for procedure-related death); median age 67 years, 320 women (40.1%), 53 with genetically confirmed FAP (6.6%); median follow-up 33 months (IQR 6.75-60)","bottom_line":"The largest papillectomy cohort to date (798 patients, 22 Japanese centres) shows that histologic R0 is achieved in only half of cases even when en bloc resection looks technically successful, and that recurrence reaches 20% at 3 years overall and still 11% after R0 - so surveillance is needed regardless of margin status; but recurrence here includes early residual disease, the adenocarcinoma category follows Japanese rather than Western criteria, and the R0-subgroup risk factors come from too few events to act on.","funding":"Not stated; study registered UMIN000040288 and approved by the Keio University Hospital ethics committee. Multiple author financial relationships declared, including lecture fees and research support from Boston Scientific Japan, Fujifilm, Olympus Marketing, Gadelius Medical and others."}}
files.new: {"16111953":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors state only that the findings 'suggest' a protective effect and that future large-scale studies are required to confirm the benefit","They note there are no data on how long the duct should be stented"],"critique":["Nineteen patients and three events cannot establish an effect. The nominally significant p = 0.02 comes from a 3-versus-0 comparison, and the intention-to-treat analysis the authors themselves perform is frankly negative (p = 0.3) - a result that should have been the headline rather than a mid-paper aside","Stopping early at an interim look triggered by a high event rate in the control arm is the classic route to an overestimated treatment effect; no alpha adjustment is applied, and the trial has roughly a fifth of its planned sample","The three analyses presented (per protocol excluding the failed placement, as-treated, intention-to-treat) give p = 0.05, 0.02 and 0.3 from 19 patients; reporting the most favourable as the result is selective","Single endoscopist, single centre, single operator technique - specifically en bloc snare without a submucosal cushion so as to include the sphincteric musculature - which the authors argue reduces later cannulation-related pancreatitis. The result therefore cannot be separated from one operator's method, and no learning-curve or centre-effect data exist","Patients were blinded but outcome ascertainment depended on patients reporting pain and then having enzymes checked; the endoscopist was necessarily unblinded, and whether the 24-hour telephone assessor's blinding was maintained for the stented patients who returned for fluoroscopy and stent removal is doubtful","Allocation by card from a sealed envelope without blocking or stratification produced unequal arms (11 vs 8) and a 9-year age difference between groups in a 19-patient trial; concealment by opaque envelope is weaker than central randomisation","The outcome window was only 24 hours, so delayed pancreatitis, bleeding, perforation, papillary stenosis and recurrence - the complications that matter over the longer term - were not captured at all","Electrosurgical generator changed during the study (Meditron to ERBE) and all three pancreatitis cases occurred with the ERBE device; generator is therefore confounded with time and potentially with allocation, and is not adjusted for","Pancreatitis was defined as threefold enzyme elevation with pain but enzymes were measured only in symptomatic patients, so asymptomatic hyperamylasaemia and milder events were differentially unascertained","The companion randomised trial in this depot (Lee 2016) found 18% versus 13% pancreatitis with wire-guided versus conventional papillectomy despite 100% stent success in the wire-guided arm, and the later ESGE guideline rates prophylactic stenting as moderate-quality evidence drawing on larger series - so this trial's 0% stented pancreatitis rate is almost certainly an artefact of its size"],"n":"19 patients enrolled and randomised (11 assigned to stent, 8 to no stent); final stent placement achieved in 10, so analysis compared 10 stented with 9 unstented patients","bottom_line":"The first and still most-cited randomised trial of prophylactic pancreatic stenting after snare ampullectomy, reporting 33% versus 0% pancreatitis, but it enrolled only 19 patients, was stopped early at an interim look, and lost statistical significance on its own intention-to-treat analysis - it is a signal consistent with a protective effect rather than proof of one.","funding":"Not stated"},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The paper carries no limitations section; but nine of eleven main recommendations are strong on low-quality evidence, its advice against molecular testing has since been reversed by the pathology consensus, and it gives no guidance on indeterminate margins."},"34529357":{"kind":"review","limitations":["The authors state that long-term efficacy and safety data for endoscopic therapy in the duodenum and at the ampullary site are almost entirely absent, that 6 of the 7 studies published in the preceding decade were single-centre retrospective series with at most 49 subjects, and that the absence of prospective international data makes the true effect of endoscopic therapy on prevention of duodenal surgery, cancer development and survival impossible to determine","No comparative studies exist between endoscopic therapy and surveillance with or without prophylactic surgery, nor between different endoscopic and surgical therapies","Guidelines on management of duodenal adenomas in adenomatous polyposis are mainly based on expert opinion because studies on clinical management are scarce","Long-term data on cancer risk in MAP patients with apparently less severe disease are hardly available, yet surveillance intervals follow the FAP recommendations","The authors explicitly suggest that given the absence of evidence on long-term efficacy, it may be time to reconsider the use of endoscopic therapy in FAP patients"],"critique":["This is a narrative review presented with the trappings of a systematic one - a PubMed search string, a screened count of 2277 and an included count of 137 - but there is no second reviewer, no inclusion/exclusion protocol, no PRISMA flow, no risk-of-bias appraisal and no quantitative synthesis.
