after exclusions 569 papillectomy (40.0% of database papillectomies) and 63 surgical ampullectomy (25.1%) were analysed, with 62 matched pairs; median follow-up 21 months (IQR 10-47)","bottom_line":"The largest comparison of endoscopic papillectomy with transduodenal surgical ampullectomy shows that a third of procedures in both arms were done for the wrong indication (non-neoplastic histology or advanced cancer), that surgery achieves higher initial R0 (90% vs 73%) with far lower recurrence after R0 (3.2% vs 16%) but at 7 times the procedure time and 11 extra hospital days, and that papillectomy fails in two-thirds of T1 cancers; but the matched analysis pairs the entire surgical population with a 1-in-9 selection of endoscopic patients, follow-up was twice as long in the surgical arm, and surveillance intensity differed, so the recurrence gap is inflated by design.","funding":"The authors have not declared a specific grant for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors. Multiple author disclosures including honoraria from FUJIFILM and Falk Foundation and institutional consultancies with Boston Scientific, Cook Medical and Pentax Medical. Ethics approval from the University of Leipzig (455/18-ek)."},"39831703":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective multi-institutional data with the usual biases; overall statistical power remained low because of disease rarity despite multiple centres","The small sample prevented splitting into derivation and validation cohorts, so the proposed score has not undergone formal validation","Ampullary lesions were not separated from duodenal lesions involving the periampullary region, although no outcome difference was found between them","Not every patient was tested genetically for FAP, MUTYH-associated polyposis or other mutations, though all underwent colonoscopy and family history assessment","Sampling bias is acknowledged because the cohort consists only of non-FAP periampullary adenomas that went on to pancreatoduodenectomy; the high malignancy rate reflects selection of high-risk cases by tumour size and location, and the true denominator - including patients managed by endoscopic mucosal resection or transduodenal resection - is unclear","A prospective study to identify the true denominator may not be feasible given the low incidence"],"critique":["The three risk strata are reported with mutually inconsistent numbers: the abstract gives low risk n = 26, intermediate n = 59, high n = 26 with rates 10.3%, 44.1% and 88.2%; the results text gives 11.5%, 41.7% and 84.6%; Table 4 gives 3/29, 26/59 and 30/34. Three different sets of denominators for the paper's central output means the score's calibration cannot be verified from the published data","The score was derived and evaluated in the same 127 patients with no split-sample, bootstrap or cross-validation, no c-statistic, no calibration plot and no sensitivity or specificity at any threshold. An OR of 77.5 for the high-risk group (CI 15.9-375.9) is the signature of an in-sample fit, and the paper's own concession that validation was impossible should preclude clinical use","The denominator problem the authors acknowledge is fatal to the score's intended purpose: everyone in the cohort had a Whipple, so the score is calibrated on the subset already judged to need resection. A patient weighing resection against endoscopic surveillance is by definition outside this population, and applying a 46% baseline malignancy rate to them would badly overestimate risk - exactly the misuse the shared-decision framing invites","Two of the four score components are proxies for obstruction, not for neoplastic progression: 'any preoperative symptom' (worth 2 points) is a list including fatigue, nausea and dark urine, and common bile duct dilation of 9 mm or more. Jaundice and biliary stenting were dropped from the model as redundant with symptoms, which concedes the point - the score largely measures whether the lesion is obstructing, and the discussant at the meeting objected that a jaundiced patient with no other factor scores only 1-2","The inverse complication relationship is presented as a feature of the score but has a simpler explanation the paper does not address: patients with benign pathology had soft, non-atrophic glands and non-dilated ducts because they had no obstructing cancer, and fistula risk follows gland texture and duct size. Adjusting for duct size and texture in the final model does not remove this, because the same obstruction physiology that lowers fistula risk is what the score is detecting","The complication finding only becomes significant after the three prespecified strata are collapsed at score 3 - across the strata as defined it was non-significant (p = 0.11) with the intermediate and high groups indistinguishable (27.1% vs 29.4%). Choosing the dichotomy that yields p = 0.047 after the three-group comparison failed is a post hoc cut-point","Preoperative dysplasia grade carries 2 of the 6 points but was read by local pathologists at 8 centres over 12 years, with no central review and no interobserver data - and the invited discussants specifically questioned whether a pathologist seeing roughly one such case per year can reliably separate high- from low-grade dysplasia","Volume was extremely low: 127 patients across 8 institutions over 12 years, about 1.3 cases per centre per year, so biopsy technique, number of biopsies, prior attempted endoscopic resection and pathology interpretation almost certainly varied in ways that cannot be modelled - a point the discussants raised and the authors do not rebut with data","EUS findings are absent from the entire paper despite both discussants noting that these are major centres where EUS would be routine; omitting the modality that best assesses intraductal extension and depth from a preoperative risk score is a substantial gap, and no explanation is given","Lesion size was missing for 27 of 127 patients (21%) and was then excluded from the score on the grounds that it did not differ between groups - a conclusion drawn from data with a fifth missing and no imputation","Black race was associated with benign final pathology (26.5% vs 11.9%) and with a different risk profile, in a cohort where race also tracked with symptoms and stenting; no analysis addresses whether differential access to earlier endoscopic diagnosis is embedded in the score's components","The 46.4% malignancy rate is compared with the same group's earlier single-centre figure of 29%, with no explanation for the difference other than cohort composition - which again points to the selection the score cannot escape"],"n":"127 patients of 189 reviewed; median age 65 years (34-89), 57 men (44.9%); 82 (64.6%) preoperative duodenal adenoma and 45 (35.4%) ampullary adenoma, with ampullary involvement in 84 of 119 (70.6%); 59 (46.4%) had malignancy on final pathology","bottom_line":"Confirms in the largest surgical series that nearly half of sporadic periampullary adenomas taken to pancreatoduodenectomy harbour cancer and that patients with benign final pathology paradoxically suffer threefold more major complications, and proposes a 0-6 malignancy risk score from age, bile duct diameter, symptoms and high-grade dysplasia; but the score is derived and tested in the same 127 already-resected patients with no validation, its published strata carry three inconsistent sets of numbers, and two of its four components are proxies for biliary obstruction.","funding":"National Cancer Institute of the NIH award K12 CA237806 (Emory K12 Clinical Oncology Training Program, Dr Shah); Contardi Research Fellowship; Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Awards UL1 TR002378. Nothing to disclose for the study; disclosures outside its scope include grant funding from Cantargia AB and consultancies with Intera Oncology, Stryker Medical and Intuitive Surgical."},"40729532":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The Delphi methodology, while the best option for reaching consensus, carries the difficulty of capturing all key issues in the literature during questionnaire development, depends on panellists' ongoing willingness to participate, and risks skewed data because those less confident about a topic may not participate","Although the stated aim was to cover all non-pancreatic cancers of the periampullary region, more recommendations relate to ampullary cancer than to common bile duct or duodenal cancer; the authors accept this imbalance as reflecting greater uncertainty and need for guidance about ampullary cancer","For a considerable proportion of the consensus questions there are fairly limited published data, so most recommendations are supported only by a low level of evidence, which the authors say highlights the early stage of knowledge about periampullary cancer","The authors state that the lack of consensus definitions and standardisation, together with high interobserver variability, has hindered consistent conclusions across studies - particularly regarding patient management including the efficacy of adjuvant chemotherapy, which remains highly controversial because of these inconsistencies"],"critique":["Almost every recommendation is graded low level of evidence with a weak form of recommendation, or rests on expert opinion alone. This is honest, but it means a document that will be used to standardise reporting worldwide is in substance a codification of the opinions of 43 experts, most of them from the pathology study groups that initiated it","THE PROCESS METRICS PROMISED ARE NOT REPORTED. The methods describe an independent Jury Committee calculating a 'Quality Score' using the AGREE II tool across 23 items and six domains, and an audience vote on each recommendation at the Brescia meeting. Neither result appears anywhere in the paper - no AGREE II score, no domain breakdown, no audience agreement percentages. The quality-assurance apparatus is described but its findings are withheld","The Delphi convergence is itself a weak signal: 33 of 57 recommendations reached 80% agreement in round one and the rest were revised by the responsible expert team according to the dissenting comments and re-voted until they passed. Revising a statement until it achieves consensus guarantees consensus; the final 50 of 51 figure measures iteration, not agreement on the original propositions","The 30% threshold for calling a tumour 'mixed' subtype has no stated derivation. It is a cut-point that will determine subtype assignment in a large fraction of cases - and the consensus itself cites that about 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed - yet no data, reproducibility study or sensitivity analysis is offered for choosing 30% over 10% or 50%","Renaming the hybrid category 'tubular-NOS' is a nomenclature change, not a solution. The underlying problem documented in this depot - that five pathologists agree on morphological subtype at kappa 0.39 with full agreement in 23% of cases - is unaddressed: no interobserver reproducibility study of the new definitions is reported or planned, so the consensus standardises the words without demonstrating that the categories can be applied consistently","The consensus states plainly that the prognostic and predictive role of subtype is unclear because of inconsistent historical definitions, yet it simultaneously retains subtyping as a required element of the pathology report and advises subtyping on biopsy where subtype 'may affect treatment'. If subtype has no established treatment implication, there is no situation in which that condition is met","Reflex MMR testing is recommended on the grounds that prevalence is 'comparable to that of colorectal cancer and is also independent on the subtype', but the supporting evidence is graded low and the two papers in this depot give prevalences of 15% in unselected non-medullary ampullary carcinoma and 4.3% in early-onset ampullary cancer - neither of which is clearly comparable to colorectal, and neither of which is cited as a prevalence estimate in the recommendation","Tumour budding is recommended as prognostically stronger than T stage and nodal metastasis, a strong empirical claim resting largely on work from the same institutional tradition that produced the ampullary classifications, with no multi-institutional validation, no reproducibility data for the 3-foci-per-200x-field threshold, and the acknowledged problem that biopsies may not contain the invasive front where budding must be assessed","229 of 37061 screened articles (0.6%) were selected, with allocation of articles to anonymous expert teams but no stated inclusion criteria, no risk-of-bias appraisal of the 229, no PRISMA flow diagram in the main text and no evidence tables - so the SIGN framework is invoked without the apparatus that makes it auditable","The anatomic definitions, which are the document's most valuable contribution, are operationalised in terms of tumour 'epicentre' and 'minimal involvement' without quantitative thresholds except in the earlier Adsay scheme they derive from; given that this literature's own data show that 21% of cases labelled ampullary are reclassified on strict review, the definitions need a reproducibility study more than they need wider adoption","The panel is heavily weighted towards pathology (initiated by ISGACA with ISGPP as steering committee), and the multidisciplinary part generated only 17 of 51 recommendations; the oncological questions that clinicians most need settled - whether subtype should guide adjuvant therapy, what to do with a T1 cancer after papillectomy - are declared unresolved rather than addressed","The consensus correctly identifies that inconsistent definitions have made the adjuvant chemotherapy literature uninterpretable, which is the strongest argument in this depot against acting on the Bolm-versus-Ecker dispute; but it stops at saying standardised future studies are needed and offers no interim guidance"],"bottom_line":"The first international consensus to define precisely what counts as ampullary carcinoma, to retire the term 'periampullary' as a diagnosis, to set a 30% threshold for the mixed subtype and rename the hybrid group 'tubular-NOS', to make mismatch repair testing reflex, and to state explicitly that the prognostic and predictive value of intestinal-versus-pancreatobiliary subtype remains unclear because the historical literature used inconsistent definitions - which is the key caveat for any pathway claiming subtype should guide adjuvant therapy; but almost every recommendation is low-evidence or expert opinion, the promised AGREE II quality score and audience vote are never reported, and no reproducibility study accompanies the new definitions.","funding":"Amsterdam Gastroenterology Endocrinology Metabolism (AGEM), Amsterdam, The Netherlands; the authors declare no conflicts of interest"},"41192607":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design over a 10-year period across 22 institutions, which may introduce missing data and selection bias","Treatment strategies - papillectomy technique, surveillance intervals and argon plasma coagulation use - varied by institution and over time because standardised guidelines were not consistently available; the authors stratified analysis by treatment period to address this","Only high-volume centres with expert teams were included, limiting generalisability","R0 margin status was assessed locally at each institution rather than centrally, which may introduce variability, although recurrence rates after R0 were comparable to other large studies","T1a and T1b adenocarcinomas were not differentiated, so prognosis by tumour stage could not be examined"],"critique":["The hazard ratios differ between the abstract/discussion and Table 2 for the same comparisons (Rx 2.30 [1.44-3.68] versus 2.38 [1.49-3.81]; R1 2.95 [1.85-4.71] versus 2.95 [1.87-4.66]). The discrepancy is small but it means two different models or datasets were in play and neither is identified","The central finding - recurrence after R0 - is partly a definitional artefact of Japanese pathological practice, which the paper itself flags: non-invasive intraepithelial neoplasia is diagnosed as carcinoma in Japan but as high-grade dysplasia in the West, so 'adenocarcinoma' in the 92 cases here is not equivalent to adenocarcinoma in the Western series alongside it, and the adenocarcinoma hazard ratio cannot be transferred","Recurrence is defined as histologic confirmation of neoplastic tissue with no requirement for a prior negative surveillance endoscopy, and the median time to recurrence was 6 months (3 months after R1). That makes a large fraction of 'recurrences' residual disease, as the pattern by margin status shows - which is consistent but means the 18.3% figure is not comparable with series that excluded residual disease, including Han 2024 in this same depot","The later treatment era (2015-2020) independently predicted recurrence (HR 1.57), which the authors attribute to more procedures by operators with fewer than 20 prior cases (26.4% rising to 44.0%). Since operator experience was not itself significant, this is an unexplained period effect that could equally reflect intensified surveillance in later years - a detection artefact that would inflate the headline recurrence rate","Margin assessment was local across 22 centres with no central pathology review and no interobserver data, yet R0/R1/Rx is the paper's principal exposure; a quarter of the cohort was Rx precisely because margins could not be read, and Rx behaved almost identically to R1 at 5 years (34% each), suggesting Rx is largely undetected R1","The R0 subgroup analysis generates the paper's most quotable new risk factors from very few events, with wildly unstable estimates: argon plasma coagulation HR 6.26 (1.44-27.1) rests on 69 of 396 R0 patients having received APC, and bile duct invasion HR 4.86 (1.08-21.8) on a handful of cases. The authors correctly reinterpret APC as a marker of endoscopically suspected residual disease rather than a cause, but the abstract-level framing does not carry that caveat","The pancreatic duct invasion estimate is reported as 0.00 (0.00-infinity) - a non-estimate from a zero cell - and is then used to argue that bile duct but not pancreatic duct invasion matters, an inference the data cannot support","Patients censored at 5 years and 21 patients removed for post-papillectomy surgery for residual cancer are exactly the group at highest risk of a bad outcome; removing them from the recurrence denominator while keeping them in the 798-patient resection-status analysis means the two headline numbers (52.1% R0, 18.3% recurrence) have different populations behind them","Female sex emerged as an independent predictor in both models (HR 1.48 and 2.09) with no mechanism offered beyond one prior report; in a model with 13 covariates and 142 events this is as likely to be noise or a proxy for an unmeasured anatomical variable","Follow-up protocols 'varied by center and clinical context' with only a typical interval of 6-12 months stated, so recurrence ascertainment is non-uniform across 22 centres and 12 years - the single most important determinant of a cumulative recurrence estimate is left undocumented","The 32.5% adverse event rate with 19.4% bleeding is substantially higher than most Western series and reflects a Japanese practice of inpatient papillectomy with a 13-day median stay; the paper does not discuss whether this reflects more complete ascertainment or a different complication profile, which matters for anyone comparing the two approaches","Several authors declare lecture fees and research support from endoscope and device manufacturers, and the study was run with the national endoscopy society's guideline committee, in a paper whose conclusions support continued endoscopic surveillance and a redefinition of R0"],"n":"875 cases enrolled, 798 with pathologically confirmed ampullary adenoma or adenocarcinoma, 776 in the long-term recurrence analysis (21 excluded for surgery for confirmed or suspected residual adenocarcinoma, 1 for procedure-related death); median age 67 years, 320 women (40.1%), 53 with genetically confirmed FAP (6.6%); median follow-up 33 months (IQR 6.75-60)","bottom_line":"The largest papillectomy cohort to date (798 patients, 22 Japanese centres) shows that histologic R0 is achieved in only half of cases even when en bloc resection looks technically successful, and that recurrence reaches 20% at 3 years overall and still 11% after R0 - so surveillance is needed regardless of margin status; but recurrence here includes early residual disease, the adenocarcinoma category follows Japanese rather than Western criteria, and the R0-subgroup risk factors come from too few events to act on.","funding":"Not stated; study registered UMIN000040288 and approved by the Keio University Hospital ethics committee. Multiple author financial relationships declared, including lecture fees and research support from Boston Scientific Japan, Fujifilm, Olympus Marketing, Gadelius Medical and others."}}

files.old: { "name": "Zenocutuzumab, for NRG1 fusions", "g": "D", "when": "NCCN lists zenocutuzumab-zbco as a subsequent therapy option for NRG1 fusion-positive disease at performance status 0–2. In the eNRGy basket trial, 36 of 158 patients in the primary efficacy population had pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and all 36 were KRAS wild-type: 15 of 36 (42%, 95% CI 25–59) responded by investigator assessment and 16 of 36 (44%, 28–62) by blinded independent central review, with median duration of response 7.4 months (4.0–11.2) investigator-assessed and 9.1 months centrally. Twenty-four of 31 pancreatic patients with baseline data (77%) had a CA 19-9 fall of at least 50%.", "pref": "A patient with KRAS wild-type disease, where NRG1 fusions are enriched — in a single-institution series the median age of 10 patients with a detectable NRG1 fusion was 48.5 years, and KRAS wild-type status is the practical trigger to look.", "avoid": "Downgraded to D. Single-arm, 36 pancreatic patients inside a basket trial sized only for the pooled estimate, with a 95% CI of 25% to 59% that cannot distinguish a major advance from a modest one. No progression-free or overall survival is reported for the pancreatic subgroup, so no survival claim can be derived from it. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed response in an open-label trial with blinded central review only as a secondary endpoint, and the primary efficacy population is a post-enrolment construct — 204 treated patients become 158 evaluable, with exclusions for short follow-up falling disproportionately on early progressors. Only 9 of 47 responses across the whole trial were ongoing at a median follow-up of 7.1 months. Adverse events were mostly grade 1 or 2 with treatment-related grade 3–4 in 7%, so the risk is low — but NRG1 fusions occur in well under 1% of PDAC, no screening denominator is given, and the sponsor designed the trial, analysed the data and drafted the manuscript.", "refs": [ "39908431" ]

files.old: {"19723142":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["The authors state the overall survival pattern raises the possibility that a LARGER study would show equivocal R1 to be an intermediate prognostic group, and that larger studies are needed to settle this definitively","They argue sub-categorisation of R1 could be supported only if a clear distinction between the two R1 groups were evident, which these data do not show","Involvement of the anterior pancreatic surface, excluded from the R1 definition here, could potentially affect survival","Histological data were incomplete for a small number of cases, so the multivariable model included 155 of 163 patients","Meaningful comparison of R1 rates between centres is complicated by the lack of standardised margin terminology and of any internationally recognised pathology protocol"],"critique":["THE CONCLUSION IS DRAWN FROM A NON-SIGNIFICANT TEST, WHICH IS AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. 'No significant difference' between 57 and 71 patients (P=0.102) in a cohort with 13.9-month median survival cannot establish equivalence; the medians differ by 2.8 months and the point estimates sit between the R0 and unequivocal-R1 groups exactly as an intermediate category would. The authors concede this in the discussion but the abstract concludes the two should be 'considered synonymous'","THE COMPARISON THE RULE ACTUALLY NEEDS IS EQUIVOCAL R1 VERSUS R0, AND THAT WAS ALSO NON-SIGNIFICANT (P=0.114). The study therefore cannot distinguish equivocal R1 from either neighbour, which is a statement about power, not biology, in a cohort of only 35 R0 patients","SINGLE CENTRE, SINGLE PATHOLOGIST, RETROSPECTIVE. One consultant pathologist re-reviewed only the R0 cases, so the reclassification effort was applied asymmetrically - cases already called R1 were not re-examined for over-calling, which is the direction of error that would inflate the 79% figure","ONLY 35 R0 PATIENTS DEFINE THE REFERENCE GROUP, and their median survival of 25.4 months has a 95% CI of 10.5-40.8 months - a four-fold range. Every comparison in the paper is anchored to this unstable estimate","THE 1997-2007 ERA MEANS ONLY 27% RECEIVED ADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY, at a time when ESPAC-1 and CONKO-001 were establishing it. Margin status interacts with adjuvant therapy, and a cohort in which three quarters got no chemotherapy cannot speak to the prognostic weight of R1 in a modern pathway","MARGIN STATUS DID NOT SURVIVE MULTIVARIABLE ADJUSTMENT, which undercuts the premise that getting the R1 definition right matters prognostically. The paper treats this as a technical problem (collinearity with tumour size) rather than as evidence that margin status may be a marker of tumour burden rather than an independent determinant of outcome","THE DECISION TO EXCLUDE THE ANTERIOR SURFACE, PanIN-3, PERINEURAL AND NODAL INVOLVEMENT FROM THE R1 DEFINITION IS A SERIES OF CONVENTIONS, NOT FINDINGS. Different centres make different choices, and the paper's own argument - that the 79% rate reflects pathology protocol rather than surgical quality - applies equally to its own conventions","THE MOST IMPORTANT IMPLICATION FOR A PATHWAY IS NOT THE ONE THE PAPER EMPHASISES. If the <1 mm rule moves the R1 rate from 44% to 79% at one centre, then R0 and R1 rates reported in every neoadjuvant and adjuvant trial are a function of local pathology practice. PREOPANC (R0 71% of resected under RCPath <1 mm), ESPAC-5 (R0 14-23%), NORPACT-1 (R0 56% vs 39%) and APACT (no central pathology review, R0 76%) are not comparable to each other, and no trial in this depot reports a pathology quality-assurance measure comparable to the one described here except ESPAC5 and CONKO-007","The argument that R1 is under-reported because 60-80% of resected patients recur locally is an indirect inference: local recurrence can arise from biologically aggressive residual disease beyond any resectable margin, not only from microscopic margin positivity","Funded by Cancer Research UK with no declared conflicts, and the senior authors are the ESPAC trialists who went on to apply this definition in ESPAC-4 and ESPAC-5 - a coherent programme, but the definition and the trials that use it come from the same group"],"n":"163 pancreatoduodenectomy specimens; 128 R1 (79%), of which 57 (45% of R1) equivocal and 71 unequivocal; 35 R0","bottom_line":"This single-centre study of 163 pancreatoduodenectomies supplied the only clinical evidence for the <1 mm R1 rule by showing that 'equivocal' R1 survival (15.4 months) resembles unequivocal R1 (12.6 months) more than R0 (25.4 months), and that the rule raises the R1 rate from 44% to 79% - but the key comparison was non-significant in a small cohort, margin status did not survive multivariable adjustment, and the real lesson is that R0 rates reported across pancreatic trials are largely a function of pathology protocol.","funding":"Supported by Cancer Research UK. No conflicts of interest are declared."},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors note the optimal duration of biliary drainage before surgery has not been established, with experimental and clinical data suggesting at least 4-6 weeks is needed","Earlier randomised studies used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage, which the authors invoke to explain why their hospital stay result differs from previous trials","Older trials mixed proximal and distal bile-duct obstruction, now regarded as different diseases needing different treatment","The authors explicitly flag that with the advent of neoadjuvant chemotherapy the question becomes clinically relevant again, and that given their poor results with PLASTIC stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with METAL stents, which have higher patency and do not affect surgical outcome"],"critique":["COMPARATOR: surgery within one week of diagnosis, which required dedicated operating-room capacity guaranteed by all 13 hospitals specifically for the trial. This is the key external-validity problem: the control strategy is only available where a jaundiced patient can be operated on within seven days. A pathway that cannot deliver that has not got the comparator the trial tested, and delay without drainage is not what was studied","PLASTIC STENTS ONLY - AND THE AUTHORS SAY THIS IS THE PROBLEM. The 26% cholangitis and 30% stent-exchange rates are largely properties of plastic endoprostheses over 4-6 weeks. Self-expanding metal stents, which every neoadjuvant protocol in this depot (PREOPANC, PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1, ESPAC5) specifies or prefers, were not tested. Citing this trial against biliary drainage before neoadjuvant chemotherapy is citing it outside its evidence","NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY WAS AN EXCLUSION CRITERION, so the trial has nothing to say about the situation in which drainage is now most often needed - bridging a jaundiced patient through months of chemotherapy. NORPACT-1 stented 57% of its neoadjuvant arm and had 2 patients derailed by persistent jaundice; PREOPANC had 10 patients whose treatment was delayed by it. That is the modern question and this trial predates it","NON-RECEIPT AND CROSSOVER: 6/202 were excluded after randomisation (2 withdrew consent, 4 had out-of-range bilirubin). Two early-surgery patients had their operation cancelled and 7 drainage patients never reached surgery. Two early-surgery patients nonetheless had drainage-related complications, implying some crossover to stenting before operation","THE PRIMARY OUTCOME COUNTS DRAINAGE COMPLICATIONS AND SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS IN ONE TOTAL, WHICH GUARANTEES THE RESULT. A strategy with an extra procedure will have extra procedural complications; the informative question is whether drainage made the OPERATION safer, and on that the trial is null (RR 0.79, CI 0.57-1.11). The 39%-versus-74% headline is therefore partly definitional, and the trial is underpowered for the surgical-complication comparison it was designed around","DESIGNED FOR NON-INFERIORITY WITH A 10-PERCENTAGE-POINT MARGIN AND 94 PATIENTS PER ARM, assuming complication rates of 38% and 48%. dose groupings were therefore not fixed in advance","A reported 6-month overall survival of 100% (95% CI 100-100) in this subgroup is a sign of how selected it is: patients had to survive long enough on a tolerated dose at the right line to enter it, which is immortal-time selection rather than a treatment effect","Three exploratory 300-mg cohorts were removed from the report for 'differing end points or eligibility criteria', including the untreated-PDAC and RAS wild-type cohorts; the reader cannot see what those patients experienced","Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause occurred in 65% of patients and 48% of the 300-mg group needed dose modification, yet the discussion characterises the profile as 'mainly low-grade adverse events' on the strength of the treatment-attributed 30% figure, an attribution made by unblinded investigators","Revolution Medicines supported the study and provided medical writing through Nucleus Global; medical writing by Nucleus Global, an Inizio Company"},"42223072":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The open-label design may have influenced adverse-event reporting, treatment modifications, and the decision not to begin treatment after randomisation; treatment was not initiated in 15.1% of the chemotherapy group, mostly by patient decision","Subgroup analyses were exploratory and limited by small sample sizes, particularly for uncommon RAS subtypes and patients with no identified RAS mutation","Given the rarity of those subgroups in PDAC, subgroup results should be interpreted descriptively"],"critique":["COMPARATOR: investigator's choice from gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, modified FOLFIRINOX, FOLFOX or liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil, given per local prescribing practice. A median overall survival of 6.6 months in that arm is at the lower end of published second-line PDAC outcomes, and because regimen choice and dosing were unconstrained the control arm's quality is not auditable from this report","NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT is the single most important asymmetry: 15.1% of the chemotherapy arm versus 2.8% of the daraxonrasib arm never started treatment, a five-fold difference. The authors attribute most of it to patient decision in an open-label trial, but patients who never start intravenous chemotherapy and are then counted in its intention-to-treat survival curve depress the comparator; no sensitivity analysis excluding or reweighting these patients is presented","Some chemotherapy-arm patients are stated to have become ineligible (ECOG above 1) between randomisation and treatment, which means the arms were not clinically equivalent at the moment treatment began — a problem an oral agent started the same day does not face","The primary efficacy population was RAS G12, with positive key secondary endpoints in the overall randomized population. files.new: {"19723142":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["The authors state the overall survival pattern raises the possibility that a LARGER study would show equivocal R1 to be an intermediate prognostic group, and that larger studies are needed to settle this definitively","They argue sub-categorisation of R1 could be supported only if a clear distinction between the two R1 groups were evident, which these data do not show","Involvement of the anterior pancreatic surface, excluded from the R1 definition here, could potentially affect survival","Histological data were incomplete for a small number of cases, so the multivariable model included 155 of 163 patients","Meaningful comparison of R1 rates between centres is complicated by the lack of standardised margin terminology and of any internationally recognised pathology protocol"],"critique":["THE CONCLUSION IS DRAWN FROM A NON-SIGNIFICANT TEST, WHICH IS AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. 'No significant difference' between 57 and 71 patients (P=0.102) in a cohort with 13.9-month median survival cannot establish equivalence; the medians differ by 2.8 months and the point estimates sit between the R0 and unequivocal-R1 groups exactly as an intermediate category would. The authors concede this in the discussion but the abstract concludes the two should be 'considered synonymous'","THE COMPARISON THE RULE ACTUALLY NEEDS IS EQUIVOCAL R1 VERSUS R0, AND THAT WAS ALSO NON-SIGNIFICANT (P=0.114). The study therefore cannot distinguish equivocal R1 from either neighbour, which is a statement about power, not biology, in a cohort of only 35 R0 patients","SINGLE CENTRE, SINGLE PATHOLOGIST, RETROSPECTIVE. One consultant pathologist re-reviewed only the R0 cases, so the reclassification effort was applied asymmetrically - cases already called R1 were not re-examined for over-calling, which is the direction of error that would inflate the 79% figure","ONLY 35 R0 PATIENTS DEFINE THE REFERENCE GROUP, and their median survival of 25.4 months has a 95% CI of 10.5-40.8 months - a four-fold range. Every comparison in the paper is anchored to this unstable estimate","THE 1997-2007 ERA MEANS ONLY 27% RECEIVED ADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY, at a time when ESPAC-1 and CONKO-001 were establishing it. Margin status interacts with adjuvant therapy, and a cohort in which three quarters got no chemotherapy cannot speak to the prognostic weight of R1 in a modern pathway","MARGIN STATUS DID NOT SURVIVE MULTIVARIABLE ADJUSTMENT, which undercuts the premise that getting the R1 definition right matters prognostically. The paper treats this as a technical problem (collinearity with tumour size) rather than as evidence that margin status may be a marker of tumour burden rather than an independent determinant of outcome","THE DECISION TO EXCLUDE THE ANTERIOR SURFACE, PanIN-3, PERINEURAL AND NODAL INVOLVEMENT FROM THE R1 DEFINITION IS A SERIES OF CONVENTIONS, NOT FINDINGS. Different centres make different choices, and the paper's own argument - that the 79% rate reflects pathology protocol rather than surgical quality - applies equally to its own conventions","THE MOST IMPORTANT IMPLICATION FOR A PATHWAY IS NOT THE ONE THE PAPER EMPHASISES. If the <1 mm rule moves the R1 rate from 44% to 79% at one centre, then R0 and R1 rates reported in every neoadjuvant and adjuvant trial are a function of local pathology practice. PREOPANC (R0 71% of resected under RCPath <1 mm), ESPAC-5 (R0 14-23%), NORPACT-1 (R0 56% vs 39%) and APACT (no central pathology review, R0 76%) are not comparable to each other, and no trial in this depot reports a pathology quality-assurance measure comparable to the one described here except ESPAC5 and CONKO-007","The argument that R1 is under-reported because 60-80% of resected patients recur locally is an indirect inference: local recurrence can arise from biologically aggressive residual disease beyond any resectable margin, not only from microscopic margin positivity","Funded by Cancer Research UK with no declared conflicts, and the senior authors are the ESPAC trialists who went on to apply this definition in ESPAC-4 and ESPAC-5 - a coherent programme, but the definition and the trials that use it come from the same group"],"n":"163 pancreatoduodenectomy specimens; 128 R1 (79%), of which 57 (45% of R1) equivocal and 71 unequivocal; 35 R0","bottom_line":"This single-centre study of 163 pancreatoduodenectomies supplied the only clinical evidence for the <1 mm R1 rule by showing that 'equivocal' R1 survival (15.4 months) resembles unequivocal R1 (12.6 months) more than R0 (25.4 months), and that the rule raises the R1 rate from 44% to 79% - but the key comparison was non-significant in a small cohort, margin status did not survive multivariable adjustment, and the real lesson is that R0 rates reported across pancreatic trials are largely a function of pathology protocol.","funding":"Supported by Cancer Research UK. No conflicts of interest are declared."},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors note the optimal duration of biliary drainage before surgery has not been established, with experimental and clinical data suggesting at least 4-6 weeks is needed","Earlier randomised studies used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage, which the authors invoke to explain why their hospital stay result differs from previous trials","Older trials mixed proximal and distal bile-duct obstruction, now regarded as different diseases needing different treatment","The authors explicitly flag that with the advent of neoadjuvant chemotherapy the question becomes clinically relevant again, and that given their poor results with PLASTIC stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with METAL stents, which have higher patency and do not affect surgical outcome"],"critique":["COMPARATOR: surgery within one week of diagnosis, which required dedicated operating-room capacity guaranteed by all 13 hospitals specifically for the trial. This is the key external-validity problem: the control strategy is only available where a jaundiced patient can be operated on within seven days. A pathway that cannot deliver that has not got the comparator the trial tested, and delay without drainage is not what was studied","PLASTIC STENTS ONLY - AND THE AUTHORS SAY THIS IS THE PROBLEM. The 26% cholangitis and 30% stent-exchange rates are largely properties of plastic endoprostheses over 4-6 weeks. Self-expanding metal stents, which every neoadjuvant protocol in this depot (PREOPANC, PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1, ESPAC5) specifies or prefers, were not tested. Citing this trial against biliary drainage before neoadjuvant chemotherapy is citing it outside its evidence","NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY WAS AN EXCLUSION CRITERION, so the trial has nothing to say about the situation in which drainage is now most often needed - bridging a jaundiced patient through months of chemotherapy. NORPACT-1 stented 57% of its neoadjuvant arm and had 2 patients derailed by persistent jaundice; PREOPANC had 10 patients whose treatment was delayed by it. That is the modern question and this trial predates it","NON-RECEIPT AND CROSSOVER: 6/202 were excluded after randomisation (2 withdrew consent, 4 had out-of-range bilirubin). Two early-surgery patients had their operation cancelled and 7 drainage patients never reached surgery. Two early-surgery patients nonetheless had drainage-related complications, implying some crossover to stenting before operation","THE PRIMARY OUTCOME COUNTS DRAINAGE COMPLICATIONS AND SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS IN ONE TOTAL, WHICH GUARANTEES THE RESULT. A strategy with an extra procedure will have extra procedural complications; the informative question is whether drainage made the OPERATION safer, and on that the trial is null (RR 0.79, CI 0.57-1.11). The 39%-versus-74% headline is therefore partly definitional, and the trial is underpowered for the surgical-complication comparison it was designed around","DESIGNED FOR NON-INFERIORITY WITH A 10-PERCENTAGE-POINT MARGIN AND 94 PATIENTS PER ARM, assuming complication rates of 38% and 48%. The observed 74% in the drainage arm far exceeded the assumption, so the trial is well powered for its headline but not for mortality (CI 0.42-1.72), resection rate (P=0.11) or surgical complications","BILIRUBIN WAS CAPPED AT 250 micromol/L, excluding the most deeply jaundiced patients - exactly those in whom drainage is most often considered unavoidable. PREOPANC used 250 micromol/L as the threshold ABOVE which it recommended drainage, so the two trials address non-overlapping populations","FIFTEEN OF 196 PATIENTS (8%) DID NOT HAVE ADENOCARCINOMA, including 5 with chronic pancreatitis and 3 with stones, and they remain in the analysis - a reminder that the preoperative diagnosis is wrong in roughly one in twelve jaundiced patients taken to pancreatoduodenectomy","THE 7% OVERALL MORTALITY IS HIGH for centres performing at least 10 resections a year and is presented as acceptable because it did not differ between arms; the authors use it to argue for centralisation, but it also means the trial's complication rates come from an era and a volume standard below modern expectations","Complications were adjudicated blind, which is a real strength, but the treating teams and patients were unblinded and readmission decisions - the outcome with the largest relative difference - are clinician-dependent"],"n":"202 randomised, 196 analysed (94 early surgery, 102 biliary drainage); 120 resections","bottom_line":"The DROP trial showed that routinely draining the bile duct with a plastic stent for 4-6 weeks before pancreatoduodenectomy nearly doubles serious complications (74% vs 39%, RR 0.54) without reducing surgical complications or mortality, so surgery within a week is preferable when it can be delivered - but it used plastic stents only, capped bilirubin at 250 micromol/L and excluded neoadjuvant chemotherapy, so it does not settle how to manage jaundice during months of preoperative treatment.","funding":"Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development, which had no access to outcome data during the trial and did not participate in analysis or manuscript preparation. No endoscopic equipment or stents were donated by manufacturers. Two authors report lecture fees from Boston Scientific and consulting or lecture fees from GI Dynamics, Covidien and Johnson & Johnson."},"21561347":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["No separate limitations section; the authors frame their own eligibility criteria as the boundary of applicability, concluding FOLFIRINOX is an option for patients under 76 with ECOG 0-1, no cardiac ischaemia and normal or near-normal bilirubin","There were fewer measurable lung metastases in the FOLFIRINOX group (19.5% vs 28.7%, P=0.05), and the authors state results were similar when adjusted for pulmonary metastases","Filgrastim was not recommended as primary prophylaxis but could be used for high-risk patients, which the authors note in describing the toxicity profile"],"critique":["The paper has no limitations section, so every point below is unstated","COMPARATOR: single-agent gemcitabine, which was the genuine standard of care in 2005-2009 - one of the few trials in this depot whose comparator was appropriate at the time it ran. Nothing in the trial addresses adjuvant or neoadjuvant use, yet PRODIGE-24, NORPACT-1, PREOPANC-2, SWOG S1505 and A021501 all justify their regimen by extrapolating from this metastatic result, an extrapolation PREOPANC-2 explicitly shows does not hold","NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT: 4/171 in the FOLFIRINOX arm and 2/171 in the gemcitabine arm never received treatment (safety populations of 167 and 169), and 8 and 7 patients had minor eligibility violations. Non-receipt was minimal and balanced - a genuine strength","THE POPULATION IS NARROW AND THE PAPER'S OWN CONCLUSION SAYS SO: age under 76, ECOG 0-1, no cardiac disease, bilirubin at or below 1.5x normal, no chronic diarrhoea, MEASURABLE disease. MPACT, run concurrently, included patients up to 88 and 8% with ECOG 2 equivalent. Real-world metastatic PDAC populations are older, frailer and frequently jaundiced; the 11.1-month median is not their expectation","PHASE 2 AND PHASE 3 PATIENTS WERE POOLED. The 88 phase 2 patients, enrolled at 15 centres under a response-rate endpoint, are included in the phase 3 survival analysis.
